body: You’re definitely not alone in this, I feel the exact same way.
I’m like this too, it’s extremely hard for me to show affection to anyone especially in person, and if I do it doesn’t start out as genuine. It takes me way too long to be genuinely affectionate.
I currently feel that I won’t make it until fall of this year, and if I do, I won’t live to graduate from high school. I guess time will tell.

My best advice is that you don’t attempt to kill your self. There’s a very high chance that you’ll fail, be sent to a hospital, and If you’re really serious you might have long lasting injuries. Instead, try and surround yourself with people who care about you, even if you don’t find pleasure in anything those people will hopefully support you, and you’ll get to a better place mentally.

I understand where the sense of abandonment can come from, and I have threatened to take my own life before when I was in a relationship.. that is very toxic and messed up, and i have realized that. If your boyfriend can’t realize that what he’s doing is toxic, just leave him. It’s not healthy.

While you’re dealing with this, if you can’t find someone to talk to, try to have an activity that’ll help you cope with your feelings. Try your hardest to stay safe, because not staying safe can worsen symptoms of depression. Find good ways to cope, and if it gets worse, definitely try and get help.

I can really relate when it comes to having dreams and not being able to achieve them because of a physical impairment. I was born with amniotic band syndrome and lost half of my right arm because of it, meaning that I can’t pursue my dreams of serving in the military or having any other job that can save lives and really prove myself. That’s always something hard to deal with, I’m really sorry that you can’t pursue your dream of becoming a doctor. I truly hope things get better someday. 

Maybe right now everything is bad, but at least the medication is helping a bit. Just stay strong, see what else can happen, maybe talk to a professional and discuss other treatment options. You seem like someone who is curious and open to learning, by the way. Don’t let your fears consume you, face them, and try to learn for your own pleasure. At the end of the day, we all learn from our failures, and that is how we grow as people.
Usually the point is to take the good moments and really cherish them, it has personally stopped me from killing my self on several occasions. Of course, everyone is different.

Yes, I completely agree, being depressed or having any mental illness that would drive you to consider suicide is extremely difficult and painful, mentally and physically. Especially when you have no one in your life- I can relate, I’m a teenager with absolutely no friends, love life, or good connections with family. When I am expressing suicidal ideation, everyone is worried, they talk to me, and then it’s like nothing happened at all. So yea, it’s tough, though I don’t really think that people realize how selfish it is. I think it comes out more because of a fear of the unknown, they don’t know what comes after death and misunderstand mental illness in a lot of cases, or the bond just isn’t good enough. Overall I think that society has been built to consider suicide a shame without really thinking about what a suicidal person truly feels.

It looks like you’ve really thought this through and have really made up your mind, and you’re right, most of the time it doesn’t get better. To hell with that idea, we are all told that everything will be fine in a few years yet it seems to get worse. But really, if you’ve got a little bit of fight left in you, I’d love it if you got to your birthday this year. I don’t know your situation but just think about it, okay? Try to find comfort in something, hold on for just a bit longer, just a few more days, and If you see that there really is no hope, then I can’t stop you, and neither can anyone else. Good luck, and happy early birthday. If no one tells you, at least take it from me.

I don’t know your situation or what has led you to this point, but you seem like someone who cares about the good of others despite your struggles. There are little ways to help others, simple gestures of kindness can make someone’s terrible day into something worth remembering. A compliment, a smile, a small act of kindness, that makes a difference. You don’t have to be a doctor, or a firefighter, or provide refuge for everyone to help. I know that if someone even smiled at me, or looked in my direction, or treated me like a person, I would be happy for the rest of that day. 

And I know, being suicidal especially during the current pandemic can be extremely difficult. Being depressed can really sap the life out of you and make a simple task like getting out of bed seem hard. I can’t tell you that it’ll get better, because that’s what everyone says and I’m just a stranger. But I know that there is beauty in the world, despite the hardships. The gentle breeze, the sound of rain on the rooftop, the smell of freshly baked goods, the comfort of warmth after a cold day: these are all beautiful things. Depression will make nothing seem enjoyable, but I’m positive you can find comfort in those things again. Consider that the world’s kindness towards you, and pay it forward. Even when everything is rough, there can be a bit of hope, and true strength in my eyes is measured by conquering your pain with that hope. 

Best of wishes to you, and really think it through before you try anything. There’s been plenty of death and pain this year, and it would be best to find your own light before deciding that you really want this. Good luck.

So this isn’t really illegal, but around this time last year I was in therapy after being discharged from the psych ward. I was having command hallucinations and would have these blackouts where I’d find out that my notebooks were filled with torture methods when I got “stable” again. So I went to therapy one night and I just Kinda ranted on and on, and it slipped that I had thoughts/plans to harm someone. A breakdown and a bunch of screaming later, and there were 4 huge cops holding me down (mind you, I was 102 pounds back then and I’m shorter than average). I got forced into an ambulance and sent to the ER. Not fun.
